note: How a built image is named, pushed and recorded. Not a JSON Schema and not under schemas/, for the reason in spec/lifecycle-v1.json. Decision 5 fixes the policy; this fixes the strings, because a reference format that does not parse fails at the one moment nothing is watching -- when ContainerProxy tries to pull.

authority.source: Deployment configuration. Never a bundle field, never derived from a content path or title.
authority.requirement: ONE authority string that both the build exporter and the host Docker daemon resolve to the same registry. This is the trap decision 5 names: `localhost:5000` inside a rootless builder is the builder's own loopback, and a Compose service name like `registry:5000` is not resolvable by the host daemon unless the host is on that network. T5 and T7 must prove a push and a COLD pull using the configured string, not two strings that happen to work in their own contexts.

repository.contentId: The content UUID in lower-case canonical form, exactly as content.id and the output descriptor use it.
repository.rationale: Keyed on identity, never on address. A rename must not move an image, and two content items must not share a repository. Registry GC and retention operate per repository, so this is also what makes 'retain every published version of this content' expressible.

tag.rationale: One tag per ATTEMPT, so a retry never overwrites the image of the attempt it retried. Tags exist for humans and for registry GC, which cannot see an untagged manifest as referenced; they are not how anything is executed.

execution_reference.rationale: Digest-pinned, and this is not a preference. DockerEngineBackend's default pull policy is IfNotPresent, so a tag whose meaning changed would never be re-pulled and a host would keep running whatever it happened to have cached. A digest names one manifest for ever. It is also what makes rollback a pointer move rather than a rebuild.
must_not_match: a tag reference, because IfNotPresent would not re-pull it

ledger.rationale: The digest alone is what executes; the tag is what registry GC can see. Recording both is what lets the collector delete an unreferenced attempt's manifest without stranding a blob that a retained version still needs.

architecture.rule: Recorded explicitly, one native Linux architecture per build.
architecture.rationale: A multi-architecture manifest produced by accident is a build whose output differs by host, which is the opposite of a digest pin. It is recorded rather than assumed so that a future arm64 deployment is an added image and not a surprise.

invalid_execution_references.registry:5000/skald/content/11111111-111: a tag reference; IfNotPresent would never re-pull it
latest, which names whatever was pushed last
digest too short to be sha256
upper-case in the content UUID; registry paths are lower-case and this would 404 on a case-sensitive registry
invalid_execution_references.registry:5000/skald/content/not-a-uuid@s: repository path is not a content UUID
invalid_execution_references./skald/content/11111111-1111-4111-8111-1: no authority, so the daemon would resolve it against its default registry
invalid_execution_references.registry:5000/skald/content/11111111-111: no digest and no tag at all; an unpinned reference resolves to whatever the daemon has or fetches, which is the failure a digest pin exists to prevent
sha512; the recorded algorithm is sha256 and a reference the daemon cannot match is a pull failure at run time

invalid_tags.latest: not an attempt id, and never used for execution
